task: EPMCDME-13933: index long marketplace assistants as token-bounded chunks via the BaseDatasourceProcessor split pipeline (per-entity numbering, deterministic ES ids, write-then-delete stale cleanup, chunk-aware unpublish, guardrails on final chunks) and dedupe marketplace search results per assistant.

component_scope.label: L
component_scope.affected: AssistantLoader, BasePlatformLoader (CHUNK_HEADER_KEY contract constant), BasePlatformDatasourceProcessor (splitter, chunk header, per-entity grouping/batching, stale-chunk cleanup, unpublish), SearchAndRerankMarketplace (over-fetch, per-assistant dedup, coverage normalisation, routing limit)
component_scope.layers: Repository/Loader, Service (indexing processor), Service (search and rerank), DB-Persistence (Elasticsearch documents)

requirements_clarity.label: L
requirements_clarity.gaps: Solution approach was not settled up front: design pivoted twice mid-flight (truncation -> custom chunking -> base-pipeline chunking); search-side behaviour for multi-chunk assistants (dedup, coverage reporting, routing limit) emerged during review rounds

technical_risk.label: L
technical_risk.risk_factors: Elasticsearch document id scheme change (<id>_<n>) with legacy single-document coexistence, write-then-delete stale cleanup via delete_by_query, unpublish deleting all chunks with progress accounting, per-entity batch fallback on embedding failures, shared base processor used by all platform datasources, search over-fetch/dedup affecting ranking and LLM source routing, guardrails moved onto final chunks
technical_risk.mitigation: Reuse of BaseDatasourceProcessor split pipeline, deterministic chunk ids, delete only after successful write, 3 review rounds (6 major findings fixed), live check 13/13, FAQ e2e verified, sanity-api harness 197 passed

key_reasoning.reason: Four components changed across loader, shared platform processor base, and marketplace search; the base processor is shared by all platform datasources, so chunking, id scheme and cleanup changes have cross-datasource reach.
Design changed twice during implementation (truncation, custom chunking, base-pipeline chunking) and search-side requirements surfaced in review, which is the rework risk the L criteria describe.

No exact precedent for multi-chunk platform entities: deterministic chunk ids, write-then-delete stale cleanup, chunk-aware unpublish, batch fallback and search dedup/over-fetch all change ES data shape and ranking behaviour, with legacy documents coexisting until reindex.
8 files (4 source, 4 test) across 4 directories with 805 insertions / 74 deletions; heavy test density from three review rounds.
